top_signals.title: “Zero Problems” Abroad, Plenty at Home: Reassessing al Sharaa’s Leadership in Syria
top_signals.summary:
In 2025, Rob Geist Pinfold wrote, “The March Massacres Show That Syria Urgently Needs Solutions, Not Sanctions,” in which he argued that sanctions relief was a major way the West could positively engage with the new Syrian government. A year later, after sanctions relief materialized and the United States removed Syria from its list of terrorism sponsors, we asked him to revisit his arguments and reassess President Ahmed al Sharaa’s leadership, both foreign and domestic. Image: Voice of America via Wikimedia CommonsIn your 2025 article, you argued that one way the West should engage with post-Assad Syria was through sanctions relief.

top_signals.title: Read This Before You Buy That TV Streaming Stick
top_signals.summary: Security experts have been sounding the alarm for years about the risks of using generic TV boxes that promise unlimited content streaming for a one-time fee, warning that they secretly rent the user's Internet connection out to strangers. But a groundbreaking new analysis finds these devices also routinely spoof themselves as mobile phones clicking ads on AI-generated websites as part of sprawling operation that seeks to defraud online merchants and advertising networks.

top_signals.title: Ten-Month Rift Keeps the Nasdaq Short of a Record
top_signals.summary: The S&P 500 closed the book on the summer selloff about a month ago and went back to setting records. The Nasdaq 100 is still tallying the bill for the season. The outstanding balance is small, but the insights it offers on this market are not.

top_signals.title: Death Toll Rises After Ferry Capsizes Off Cyprus
top_signals.summary: At least eight people died and 18 were missing after a ferry carrying around 270 passengers and crew capsized off North Cyprus on Sunday, leaving survivors clinging to its overturned hull.The privately owned ferry left the port of Kyrenia at 12:30 p.m.
